units.title: Media Preparation & Optimization

Activity 3: Media Optimization for maximum yield ● Task: “Placket-Burman” Simulation, Given a list of 10 media components (Glucose, peptone,salts,etc.), describe a strategy to find which one can increase the product yield. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Propose a statistical design to find where carbon and nitrogen ratiosmaximize the titer/concentration of the target metabolite. ● Expected Outcome: Creative and applied understanding of nutritional/environmental needs of microbes

units.title: Microbial Enzymes & Enzymatic Bioprocesses

Activity 2: Enzyme immobilization Techniques ● Task: Group discussion on various immobilisation techniques, reactors and bioproducts ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Improving biocatalytic yield using immobilized enzyme. ● Expected Outcome: Ability to understand importance of enzymatic processes.

units.title: Fermenter design, scale up & Economics

units.title: Nature of Heat Flow
units.topics: Activity 1: The "Household Heat Map" Audit ● Task: Identify and categorize the three modes of heat transfer in a common kitchen appliance (e.g., a boiling kettle or a convection oven). ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Exercise to understand the nature of heat flow quickly. ● Expected Outcome: Developing an ability to identify and apply modes of heat transfer Activity 2: Geometry Specific Heat Flow ● Task: Case-based quiz on differences between hot water pipes and tanks ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Accurate geometry specific analysis of cylindrical, spherical and rectangular surfaces for example hot/cold liquid pipes, water tanks, storage vessels, heat exchangers) ● Expected Outcome: Understanding the geometry specific heat flow and heat transfer co- efficients. Activity 3: Comparative Report Assignment ● Task: Prepare a report comparing steady and unsteady state heat transfer phenomena ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Understanding importance of steady state while writing a heat balance equation ● Expected Outcome: Ability to differentiate between steady state and unsteady state phenomena

units.title: Heat Exchanger Equipments
units.topics: Activity 1: Energy balances and LMTD ● Task: Write a complete energy balance equations for double pipe heat exchanger operating in co- current or counter current mode. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Perform a complete energy balance on a double-pipe heat exchanger to determine its required length. ● Expected Outcome: Determine the required length and area of heat exchanger. Activity 2: Numerical Solving ● Task: Solve numericals on various heat exchangers. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Determine the effective area and type of heat exchanger ● Expected Outcome: Enhance problem solving ability of students

units.title: Molecular Diffusion in Fluids
units.topics: Activity 1: Compare and analyse Heat, Mass and Momentum transfer Laws ● Task: Identify similarity and differences between Fourier’s law, Ficks Law and Newtons Law ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: How these laws are applicable in solving real life examples. ● Expected Outcome: Improve understanding on application and analogy between these laws. Activity 2: Virtual/Practical Lab – Solid-Liquid Diffusion ● Task: Perform an experiment on solid (Benzoic acid pellet) –liquid (Water) diffusion in a lab ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Determine mass transfer co-efficient of solid-liquid diffusion ● Expected Outcome: Bridge the gap between theory and practice Activity 3: Reflection Discussion ● Task: Discuss various theories of mass transfer ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Applying mass transfer principles in microbial fermentation processes. ● Expected Outcome: Insights into how internal and external factors affect rate of mass transfer

units.title: Enzyme Kinetics

units.title: Mendelian Genetics
units.topics: Activity 1: Data Analysis of Inherited Traits in a Sample Population ● Task: Survey at least 20 individuals for 3 Mendelian traits. Tabulate genotypic and phenotypic frequencies. Use Hardy-Weinberg Equation to calculate allele frequencies and analyze population equilibrium. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Applying population genetics to understand how genetic traits persist or change across generations. ● Expected Outcome: Students will develop skills in statistical genetics and interpretation of inheritance data. Activity 2: MCQ-Based Quiz on Genetic Crosses and Gene Mapping ● Task: Solve a 20-question quiz covering monohybrid/dihybrid crosses, recombination frequency, and linkage analysis. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Strengthening foundational understanding necessary for genomic diagnostics. ● Expected Outcome: Reinforcement of key concepts in classical and molecular genetics.

units.title: DNA and RNA Topology
units.topics: Activity 1: Nucleic Acid Terminology Puzzle ● Task: Solve a crossword puzzle using key terms related to DNA and RNA. Use clues based on textbook definitions and class discussions. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Difficulty in remembering and applying essential molecular biology terms. ● Expected Outcome: Improved vocabulary retention and understanding of core concepts in nucleic acid biology. Activity 2: Molecular Basis and Therapeutic Design of Synthetic mRNA in Vaccine Development ● Task: Write a brief report (150–200 words) explaining how synthetic mRNA (like that used in COVID-19 vaccines) is designed and functions inside the body. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Understanding the molecular design of RNA therapeutics used in public health. ● Expected Outcome: Students relate RNA structure and processing to real-world biomedical applications.

units.title: DNA Replication in Eukaryotes and Prokaryotes
units.topics: Activity 1: Thought Experiment – DNA Replication Without Topoisomerase ● Task: Imagine DNA replication without topoisomerase activity. Predict what will happen to the replication fork. Write a short paragraph with reasoning. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Encourages critical thinking about enzyme necessity in molecular biology. ● Expected Outcome: Understanding the mechanical stress and torsion control during replication. Activity 2: DNA Replication Flowchart ● Task: Cut out 6–8 steps of DNA replication written on paper slips. Mix them up and arrange in correct order with arrows. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Students often memorize steps without proper order or causality. ● Expected Outcome: Students internalize the logical flow of the replication process.

units.title: Transcription in Eukaryotes and Prokaryotes
units.topics: Activity 1: Viral Hijacking of Transcription ● Task: Analyze a case study on how viruses like HIV manipulate host transcription using host RNA polymerase and transcription factors. Write down your understanding about this process with diagrams. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Understanding viral control over host gene expression is key to developing antiviral strategies. ● Expected Outcome: Students will relate transcriptional regulation to real-world disease mechanisms and therapeutic challenges. Activity 2: Open Book Assessment – Compare Polymerases ● Task: Using textbook content, compare DNA polymerase I, II, and III in prokaryotes. Write their primary function, proofreading ability, and unique roles, etc. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Confusion among DNA polymerase types and their features. ● Expected Outcome: Clear distinctions between enzymes critical for replication and repair.

units.title: Translation in Eukaryotes and Prokaryotes
units.topics: Activity 1: Case Study – Antibiotics That Inhibit Protein Synthesis ● Task: Research and present how specific antibiotics (e.g., tetracycline, chloramphenicol, erythromycin) inhibit bacterial translation without affecting eukaryotic cells. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Importance of understanding molecular targets in drug design. ● Expected Outcome: Students appreciate the role of ribosomal structure in selective drug action. Activity 2: RNA World – Fact or Fiction Quiz ● Task: Students will attempt a 20-statement quiz based on concepts of RNA structure, function, and the RNA world hypothesis. For each statement, they must mark it as Fact or Fiction and correct the statement if it is false. ● Real-Life Problem Addressed: Students often memorize RNA facts but struggle to distinguish between accurate and outdated or oversimplified information. ● Expected Outcome: Students will develop critical thinking by identifying and correcting false scientific statements.
